notes.detailedSummary: On the actual genuinely nonalgebraizable surface over C((s)), with theta=DD(|tau|^2/2) and raw mass two, the draft reconstructs all-stage continuous products/Green, canonical cubic generated energy/MA/mixed products, finite FULL bounded dual, all four moving moments, comparison/clamps, actual atoms at every total graded-dimension-two point, and full generated pointwise uniqueness via two actual Gauss fibres. The 404 finite-extension preservation and fixed-bounded-probe coefficient-integrable current statements are audited independently. Essential applied primary statements/immediate units were read; named deeper conventional foundations were not recursively whole-audited. Actual native280 FINAL and different formal companion remain separate DATA. The scope is G, not an identified intrinsic E1 domain, and there is no prescribed-measure existence or nonordered compactness theorem.
notes.text:
This is an independent unverified scoped reconstruction, with no incoming correctness grant and no supplied verdict or supplied note used as a mathematical premise. It applies to K=C((s)), |s|=exp(-1/8), t=s^8, Y=(G_m^2)^an_K and the ACTUAL X=Y/<(t,2),(3,t)>. The original P16.7 is not claimed solved.

Geometry and retained foundations. The two periods translate tau=(-log|z1|,-log|z2|) by Z^2. Ordinary boxes of widths less than one give injective open quotient charts; the compact unit polyannulus covers X. Finitely many deck graphs meet bounded chart products. Conrad--Temkin4.2.3 glues the local etale-relation quotients, and4.2.4 descends the coherent diagonal ideal along a FINITE flat quasi-finite chart cover with finite fibres. It is not applied to the infinite-sheeted map Y->X. Thus X is compact good strict smooth separated boundaryless connected pure dimension two and proper.

Nonalgebraization is reconstructed rather than inferred from lack of an ample bundle. GrusonIV.5 Theorem1 gives SK^0=0 only for completed products of divisible-radius discs and unit circles. Determinants trivialize line bundles there. Fill a wide annulus by its inner disc, gluing along its inner circle with Tate--Kiehl coherent gluing (Van der Put2.14--2.16.3); induction in the number of wide factors proves Pic(P_m)=0 on P_m={|s|^m<=|zi|<=|s|^-m}. For a unit b=sum b_beta z^beta on P_m, its Gauss log norm is affine because it and its negative are convex. An interior maximizing monomial alpha agrees throughout the box, and |b_beta/b_alpha|exp((m/8)|beta-alpha|_1)<=1. Normalize successive frames by scalar monomials. Their transitions 1+g_m satisfy ||g_m||_(P_j)<=|s|^(m-j) for fixed j<m; the products and inverse tails converge. They produce a global frame, so Pic(Y)=0. Global units are scalar monomials, since a second exponent would dominate on a tropical ray.

Multipliers c_i z^(h_i), h1=(A,B),h2=(C,D), obey t^C2^D=3^At^B. Thus C=B,A=D=0 and h1=(0,k),h2=(k,0). For k!=0 choose lambda=lambda1 lambda2^(sign k), whose exponent h=(k sign k,k) has v(lambda^h)=2|k|>0. A section has coefficient recurrence a_(m+jh)=a_m c^j lambda^(-jm-hj(j+1)/2). Its negative quadratic valuation growth contradicts Laurent convergence. For k=0 at most one monomial occurs; sections with identical multipliers are proportional. The pole ideal of a meromorphic F is the coherent kernel of multiplication by its numerator modulo its denominator. Smooth regular local factoriality (Stacks0AG0), and regular/flat analytic restrictions (Ducros2.1.3(2),(5),2.1.4), make it invertible and preserve the kernel. Its global frame on Y and its product with F have the same multipliers, so Gamma(X,M_X)=K. A separated finite-type algebraic-space algebraization would be smooth proper integral dimension two by Conrad--Temkin2.3.1. Stacks086U,0BB1,0EN6,0ENA,0END identify its rational/meromorphic field on a dense scheme locus; smoothness supplies their generic/weak-associate hypotheses. Flat analytic local maps and a closed point test inject that transcendence-degree-two field into K, contradiction. This is nonalgebraization over the stated K, not over every extension.

Positivity and continuous calculus. Locally rho=|tau|^2/2, theta=DD rho; reference changes are affine unit logarithms. Saturated degree-one torus calibration gives theta^2=2 times Lebesgue measure on the reference Gauss section, raw mass M=2. Theta degenerates on residue bidiscs. C consists of continuous a whose rho+a belongs to the ENTIRE minimal CLD continuous psh sheaf (8.1.7--8.1.8), containing ordinary smooth generators and closed under local uniform limits. Recursive CLD8.5.1,8.5.3,8.5.5--6,8.7.1--4,8.8.4--5 give actual positive symmetric local products theta_a=theta+DDa, B(a,b)=theta_a wedge theta_b, MA(a)=B(a,a), gluing across the reference changes and of mass two. Positive top currents/coefficients are actual Radon measures by7.2.8--12;15.7.1 applies to separated pure-dimensional analytic spaces. No arbitrary-multiplier closedness8.6.7 is used.

The additional all-stage Green step is proved through a local positive Hilbert completion for a positive closed current T. Smooth gradients with strong limits and uniformly approximated functions form a sheaf H_T, patched by partitions and Leibniz. A uniformly zero sequence with a strong gradient limit pairs to zero with every smooth test by closedness, so its gradient limit is zero. For L_T f=DD(fT) signed Radon one obtains Q_T(f,g)=-integral f L_T g=-integral g L_T f and Q_(T,chi)(f)=1/2 integral f^2 DDchi wedge T-integral chi f L_T f. For uniformly convergent psh f_j, cutoffs chi,eta with eta=1 near supp chi and |f_j|<=B on the WHOLE supp eta give, with epsilon=||f_j-f_k|| there,
0<=Q_(T,chi)(f_j-f_k)<=epsilon^2||DDchi wedge T||_TV/2+2B epsilon||chi||infinity||DDeta wedge T||_TV.
Strong gradients therefore pass uniform limits and minimality includes every continuous stage. For continuous dpsh f,g this proves symmetric Green and Q_T(f)>=0, without an arbitrary-current pullback.

E(a)=1/3 integral a[theta^2+B(a,0)+MA(a)] is a cubic. Green gives E'(a_t)=integral(b-a)MA(a_t), E''(a_t)=-2Q_(theta_at)(b-a)<=0. E is monotone/concave, E(0)=0, E(a+c)=E(a)+2c, and
E(b)-E(a)=1/3 integral(b-a)[MA(a)+B(a,b)+MA(b)].
Every integral on this right side is positive when a<=b and is at most3(E(b)-E(a)).

Canonical generated class. G consists of ACTUAL pointwise presentations a_j in C decreasing to u with finite lower E. The functions are USC, not equivalence classes. Compact strict domination is elementary even for USC nets: if f_i decrease to f<h everywhere, h continuous finite, the increasing open sets {f_i<h} cover compact X, and finite subcover/directedness give one global late index. Compare presentations with a term of the other plus epsilon to prove canonical E(u), order preservation and energy continuity when the infimum is already generated. An identically -infinite limit contradicts the energy bound. Convex combinations are generated.

On any finite simplex the energies have degree at most three. Values at a finite unisolvent set converge, hence all coefficients converge. For bounded v in C, P_j(t)=E((1-t)a_j+tv), R_j(t)=E(ta_j) give integral v MA(a_j)=P'_j(0)+R'_j(1), canonically. Span C is a uniformly dense vector lattice: small periodic smooth perturbations separate tropical classes; a globally capped Laurent-polynomial logarithm separates different seminorms in one fibre, with a zero collar and zero branch near zeros. The identity max(A(p-q),A(r-s))=2A max((p+s)/2,(r+q)/2)-A(q+s) supplies the lattice property. Positive common mass and density give convergence against EVERY continuous test and compact-Hausdorff Riesz gives actual Radon MA(u). Polarization gives actual mixed products.

Define the FULL bounded dual D(mu)=sup_(a in C)(E(a)-integral a mu). Constants force positive mu to have mass2 if D(mu)<infinity. For u<=0, monotone convergence of a sequence presentation gives integral(-u)mu<=D(mu)-E(u), integrability and presentation L1 convergence. Bounded tangent gives D(MA(a))=E(a)-integral a MA(a). The finite coefficient D_u=lim integral a_j MA(a_j)=R'(1) first gives D(MA(u))<=E(u)-D_u, proving integrability BEFORE unbounded moments. For k>=j the cocycle bounds integral(a_j-a_k)MA(a_k)<=3(E(a_j)-E(a_k)); let k then j tend to infinity using fixed-continuous tests and established L1. Thus D_u=integral u MA(u) and D(MA(u))=E(u)-integral u MA(u). The coefficient partial_s E(tu+sv) at(1,0) equals integral v MA(u): prove it first for bounded v, then decrease its presentation, using coefficient convergence and integrability. This proves ALL FOUR moving moments for arbitrary continuous presentations of u,v, not just fixed tests. Generated first variation follows. Lipschitz ramps and moving/fixed-slot L1, then atom-free level approximation, prove nonopen comparison and max locality. Clamps u^A=max(u,-A) satisfy 1_(u>-A)MA(u^A)=1_(u>-A)MA(u); the ENTIRE contact set is excluded. For E(u)>=-C the discarded mass is <=3C/A. No discontinuous clamp is silently a continuous CLD product.

All-test estimate. For a,b,w<=0 of E>=-C, cocycle and tangent give integral(-p)MA(q)<=3C and integral(-p)B(q,r)<=6C. For f=a-b,g=(a+b)/2,h=w-g,
I(a,b)=integral(a-b)(MA(b)-MA(a))=Q_theta_a(f)+Q_theta_b(f)>=0,
Q_theta_w(f)-I/2=Q_theta_a(f,h)-Q_theta_b(f,h).
Both transgressions have the signed value -integral f DDf wedge DDh. Since |h|<=-w+(-a-b)/2, each h-slot is bounded by12C+3C+6C=21C. Direct-sum Cauchy--Schwarz gives Q_theta_w(a-b)<=I/2+sqrt(42CI). For equal generated MA, all FOUR moving moments make I_j->0 for ANY presentations, so every FIXED bounded test gradient energy tends to zero, with no common supnorm lower bound.

Actual point atoms, without scalar extension. At a total graded-dimension-two point x the support kernel is zero by Abhyankar. Completion of K(z1,z2) adds no initials; Laurent-polynomial initials generate the graded field by fractions. Select two homogeneous independent initials represented by P1,P2. Their actual image is the weighted Gauss point of arbitrary positive real radii r_i=|Pi(x)|. CLD11.6.5(c) applies at relative interior, reduced target, dimensions<=2, image graded dimension2;11.6.3 gives a compact local finite-flat rankD>0 representative with SINGLE Gauss fibre{x}. Pleasant-moment calibration14.5.2--3 gives degreeD upstairs. For psi=max(0,log|P1|/r1,log|P2|/r2), interpret each logarithm as log(|Pi|/ri). Smooth log-sum-exp gradient fills the standard simplex of area1/2; raw2! gives mass1, concentrating at the vertex. Properness and singleton fibre imply convergence against every actual continuous upstairs test to D delta_x. A global cap max(rho_a,delta+epsilon psi)-rho_a, zero on a collar, belongs to C by capped smooth logarithms and soft maxima. Its inner curvature is epsilon DDpsi, so MA(w_x)>=alpha_x delta_x with alpha_x=epsilon^2D>0. The WHOLE bounded test MA(w_x) has finite FULL dual, hence -u(x)<= (D(MA(w_x))+C)/alpha_x for u<=0,E(u)>=-C. A normalized Dirac component is NOT inferred to have finite full dual.

Classical recognition and Shilov reconstruction. Exact GR-v2 names: the ordinary smooth recognition is the UNNUMBERED Section1.2 paragraph; Proposition4.2 supplies sheaf/convex/max/decreasing-NET closure; Theorem6.1 is local maximum; Theorem6.4 is affinoid Shilov maximum, NOT USC regularization. The native404 interchanged labels are corrected, not inherited. The theorem's maximum-set wording 'since h is continuous' is harmlessly replaced by its stated USC hypothesis. Uniform closure follows from h_j+3*2^-j for errors<=2^-j; minimality recognizes ALL continuous stages and decreasing closure recognizes generated local weights, under all analytic curve/complete extension tests. GR6.3 and Abhyankar make ALL affinoid Shilov points total full dimension2. For a local classical weight q,
q(x)=inf_(A affinoid neighbourhood of x) max_(Gamma_A)q.
Maximum gives one inequality, USC and arbitrarily small affinoid neighbourhoods the other, including q(x)=-infinity. All boundaries vary; no fixed skeleton is being used.

Full generated uniqueness is independently reconstructed as follows. A full1 point q on Gm over complete F lifts after a FINITE E/F to a Gauss disc eta_(a,R),0<R<=r=|z|. For classification only, lift to the completed algebraic closure; CLD13.8.8(d) preserves full graded dimension via finite extension over the graded compositum. Nested discs with empty intersection have every linear-factor initial a base constant, hence graded dimension0; radius0 is rigid of dimension0. Thus a positive-radius disc exists, and an algebraic centre within R gives finite E. Its path eta_(a,t),R<=t<=r has constant |z|=r, finite log-length log(r/R), and ends at eta_(0,r). The moment z-a has local degreeONE and primitive calibrationONE (14.5.2--3). Cauchy--Schwarz bounds squared endpoint difference by log-length times the positive cutoff curve gradient energy. Finite varying-ground-field integration15.3.1/16.1.1 has factorONE, not[E:F].

For nonconstant Laurent P(z2), CLD18.6.1--2 at boundaryless separated equidimensional hypotheses identifies T=DD max(0,log(|P|/rP)) with the ACTUAL integration current of P^-1(Gauss_rP). The fibre is disjoint Gm_Lnu, finite Lnu over its Gauss field; characteristic0 makes P(z2)-T squarefree. Viewing a component over the smaller Gauss field introduces kappa=[Lnu:F0]>0 by14.4.3, a DIFFERENT operation from normalized finite ground-field extension. A bounded global cap has theta_w=epsilon T on an inner region. Thus Q_theta_w(h)>=epsilon*kappa times cutoff actual curve energy. Applying this to differences of ambient smooth strong/uniform approximants proves strong curve convergence and extends the endpoint inequality to CONTINUOUS presentation differences. No arbitrary-current pullback or unbounded divisor restriction occurs.

At full2 x, tower additivity and relative Abhyankar imply its z2 projection q2 is full1 and x is relative full1 over H(q2). Select Laurent P(z2) with transcendental initial, so P(q2) is Gauss and H(q2) finite over its Gauss field. In ACTUAL fibre Gm_H(q2)(z1) the first finite path ends at xi1, the z1 Gauss point over q2, at the same original norm tuple. The fixed P(z2)-cap controls presentation endpoint differences tending to0. Xi1 is total full2 and projects z1 to eta_K,r1. In the SECOND ACTUAL fibre Gm_H(eta_K,r1)(z2) another finite path ends at the joint Gauss point; its z1-cap controls the second endpoint difference. Point atoms make u,v finite at all three endpoints, so actual u-v agrees with its joint-Gauss value. Coordinate-radius finite paths in actual fibres connect all reference Gauss points using finitely many chart pieces. Consequently one constant holds at every full2 point; all-Shilov reconstruction makes u=v+c POINTWISE including poles. Sup0 removes c. No varying Shilov section is declared analytic (GR5.7 warning respected).

404 claims independently audited. Finite scalar extension preserves continuous products and E by normalized integration; pulling presentations passes to G. In the finite Galois case upstairs measures are invariant, each fibre H(x) tensor F has one Galois orbit, and averaging continuous tests descends through the proper quotient. Thus invariant measures are determined by pushforward, and equal MA downstairs gives equal MA upstairs. No arbitrary lifted-measure full-dual or infinite extension claim follows. For a compact smooth(1,1) probe alpha and FIXED bounded w, finitely many rational chart unit moments can be approximated by Laurent quotients below each unit's positive minimum norm. Ultrametricity gives EXACT equal norms/moments. Smooth convex capped logs of their numerator/denominator polynomials supply bounded p_i whose Hessians dominate both signs of alpha on the inner charts. A finite partition gives |alpha wedge theta_w|<=sum c_i B(p_i,w)<=sum2c_i MA((p_i+w)/2). Full dual therefore supplies actual coefficient integrability of u theta_w, and presentations converge coefficientwise L1. Green and vanishing all-test gradient energies give DD(u theta_w-v theta_w)=0 for EVERY FIXED bounded w. Constants/tests depend on w and alpha; there is NO uniform cap-to-divisor limit.

notes.detailedSummary: For ordered nonpositive a<=b and bounded w with E>=-C, integral(b-a)MA(w)<=F_C(E(b)-E(a)), where F_C(d)=3d+sqrt(12C*(9d/2+sqrt(126Cd))) tends to zero. It extends to ordered actual generated weights after fixed shifts, including every full-dimensional point via bounded test atoms. A sequence with energies approaching the real infimum of a decreasing net represents its exact infimum at every full point; all-affinoid-Shilov reconstruction gives the exact representative including poles. No cofinal sequence, metrizability, intrinsic-domain identification or arbitrary-measurable-net monotone convergence is assumed. The same original sequence-generated class is retained. Nonordered energy-sublevel compactness and prescribed-measure existence are not proved.
notes.text:
This new scoped theorem uses the independently reconstructed actual calculus, point atoms and all-Shilov determination of the earlier own note n1. It does not use any supplied note as a premise. All hypotheses, normalization and definitions of K,X,theta,C,G,E,MA,B and full dual are exactly those of n1: actual nonalgebraizable X, raw positive mass2, ALL continuous stages, pointwise sequence-generated finite-energy weights, and no measure support restriction.

Quantitative theorem. If a,b,w in C are nonpositive, a<=b, and E(a),E(b),E(w)>=-C for C>=0, write delta=E(b)-E(a)>=0. Then
0<=integral(b-a)MA(w)<=F_C(delta),
F_C(d)=3d+sqrt(12C*(9d/2+sqrt(126Cd))).
In particular F_C(d)->0 as d->0; no common supnorm lower bound is required. At a positive atom alpha of the actual bounded MA(w), the same inequality gives 0<=b(x)-a(x)<=F_C(delta)/alpha.

Complete derivation. Let f=b-a>=0. The positive energy cocycle yields integral f MA(a)<=3delta. Positive Green gives I(a,b)=Q_theta_a(f)+Q_theta_b(f)>=0, while positivity of MA(b) gives I<=integral f MA(a)<=3delta. Put T=theta_w+theta_a and k=w-a. Actual symmetric products give MA(w)-MA(a)=DD(kT). Thus Green and Hilbert Cauchy--Schwarz imply
integral f MA(w)=integral f MA(a)-Q_T(f,k)
<=3delta+sqrt(Q_T(f)*Q_T(k)).
The n1 all-test bound and Q_theta_a(f)<=I give Q_T(f)<=3I/2+sqrt(42CI). Also Q_T(k)=I(a,w)<=integral|a-w|(MA(a)+MA(w))<=12C: expand |a-w|<=-a-w and use the four3C moment bounds. Substitute I<=3delta to obtain the stated F_C. Every current is fixed positive closed at this step, and all multipliers are bounded continuous dpsh. The atom bound uses positivity of the entire actual measure; it makes no assertion that its normalized Dirac component has finite full dual.

Generated ordered version. Suppose u<=v in G, u,v<=B and E(u),E(v)>=L. Take ANY continuous presentations A_j decreasing to u and B_j decreasing to v, and replace B_j by max(A_j,B_j). This is decreasing in C, has exact limit v and dominates A_j. Compact strict domination discards finitely many terms to give both<=B+1. Subtract B+1 from both and independently sup(w) from the fixed bounded test; these shifts preserve the differences and MA(w). A single
C>=max(0,2(B+1)-L,-E(w-sup(w)))
works for all terms. Canonical energies give delta_j->E(v)-E(u), and full dual of MA(w) gives actual L1 convergence of both presentations. The integral estimate passes to u,v. At full-dimensional x, n1 point atoms give finite actual values, so the point estimate also passes. In particular ordered u<=v with equal E have equal values at all full2 points, and all-Shilov reconstruction gives u=v POINTWISE including poles.

We reconstruct the countable representation lemma explicitly so no supplied countable-closure grant enters. Suppose u_k in G decrease, L=inf E(u_k)>-infinity. Choose their presentations f_(k,j), enumerate ALL pairs as h_1,h_2,..., and put u=inf_k u_k=inf_m h_m. Set epsilon_n=2^-n and r_n=sum_(ell>n)epsilon_ell=2^-n. Compact strict domination selects k_n>=max(n,k_(n-1)) with u_(k_n)<h_m+epsilon_n for all m<=n. Since u_(k_n)<=u_(k_(n-1))<=v_(n-1), it also lies strictly below v_(n-1)+epsilon_n. Select a sufficiently late presentation term v_n=f_(k_n,j_n) below all these finitely many continuous bounds. Those bounds are comparisons only; their minimum is NEVER claimed psh. Then a_n=v_n+r_n in C strictly decreases because epsilon_n+r_n-r_(n-1)=0. It dominates u, and for every fixed m is eventually below h_m+epsilon_n+r_n. Its ACTUAL pointwise limit is therefore u, including poles. E(a_n)>=E(u_(k_n))>=L by order and the positive constant rule. Thus u in G. Order gives E(u)<=L; compact strict domination against a presentation term of u plus epsilon gives L<=E(u). Hence E(u_k) decreases to E(u).

ARBITRARY decreasing-net closure theorem. Let (u_i) indexed by ANY directed I decrease in G and have L=inf_i E(u_i)>-infinity. Restrict to a tail i>=i0. Its infimum and energy infimum agree with the originals, by directedness, and u_i<=u_i0 supplies a common finite upper bound B. Recursively choose i_n>=i_(n-1) with E(u_i_n)<=L+2^-n: choose an energy-near-infimum index and a directed upper bound. Countable closure gives v=inf_n u_i_n in G and E(v)=L. This sequence is NOT asserted cofinal in I.

Fix any tail index i and any total full2 point x. For each n choose j_n>=i,i_n. Then u_j_n<=u_i_n and u_j_n<=u_i, and
0<=E(u_i_n)-E(u_j_n)<=2^-n.
The generated ordered atom estimate uses a single C_x depending only on B,L,w_x, independent of i,n,j_n, and gives
0<=u_i_n(x)-u_j_n(x)<=F_(C_x)(2^-n)/alpha_x ->0.
All these point values are finite by n1. Since u_j_n(x)<=u_i(x), passage to the limit gives v(x)<=u_i(x) for every i. Conversely u=inf_i u_i<=v. Thus u=v at ALL full2 points, without countable cofinality or a countable test set.

The actual u is USC because infima of USC functions are USC. GR Proposition4.2(4) gives classical psh of the local weights rho+u by its decreasing-NET rule; rho+v is classical as generated. Every affinoid Shilov point is full2. The exact all-Shilov formula q(x)=inf_A max_GammaA q gives u=v on EVERY point, including poles. Consequently the arbitrary net infimum belongs to the SAME original SEQUENCE-generated G and E(u_i) decreases to E(u)=L. This is actual representative construction, not a coordinate product limit or an abstract dual representative.

Directed operator and moving-moment continuity. For any finite collection of decreasing energy-bounded nets, use the common directed product index. Each fixed convex combination decreases with a finite lower energy bound by concavity, so the new theorem gives its actual generated limit and canonical energy continuity. At a finite unisolvent cubic interpolation set all values converge, hence coefficients converge. The actual first-variation coefficient identities of n1 yield MA convergence against C, ALL FOUR moving MA moments and mixed polarizations. Span C is uniformly dense in C(X), and mass is always2, so weak convergence holds against EVERY continuous analytic-space test. For example integral u_i MA(v_i)->integral u MA(v), as do all self/cross moments; fixed-u mixed tests follow by treating u as a constant net.

Arbitrary-support finite-full-dual net L1 continuity. For any positive Radon mu of raw mass2 and D(mu)<infinity, n1 proves integrability of each generated weight and SEQUENCE presentation L1 convergence. Let a_m decrease continuously to the actual u. For fixed m and epsilon>0, the strict continuous majorant a_m+epsilon dominates u everywhere. Compact strict domination of the NET gives eventually u<=u_i<a_m+epsilon. Thus
0<=integral(u_i-u)mu<=integral(a_m-u)mu+2epsilon.
Choose m, then epsilon, then a late net index. This proves integral|u_i-u|mu->0. The set{u=-infinity} is a common mu-null set by finite full dual; outside it every u_i>=u is finite. No uncountable union of null sets is used. General measurable-net monotone convergence would be false: the net 1_[0,1]\F over finite subsets F decreases to0 while each Lebesgue integral is1. Our proof supplies actual continuous majorants and avoids that error; this diagnostic is not a psh counterexample.

Scope and evidence. Downward filtered generated families can be indexed by order and are also covered. Energy selection need not give a cofinal subset; it gives the same actual weight through quantitative order separation. This removes the previous arbitrary-decreasing-net representation gate. It does not compactify a NONORDERED energy sublevel: minima and inf-tail weights are not known psh/generated, so a rooftop/envelope input is still missing. Nor does it recognize a sufficient intrinsic E1 domain, produce actual obstacle envelopes/orthogonality, construct a variational maximizer or solve EVERY prescribed arbitrary-support finite-full-dual measure. Finite full dual is a noncircular criterion and is not replaced by mu=MA(u).

The full proof and the independently audited inputs appear in scoped-paper.tex (Theorems gap/net and their corollaries) and ENTIRE proof-companion.txt, with source-application-reading-ledger.txt/json and unchanged original-residual.txt. Newly authored verify_progress.py checks only finite rational algebra: eight cubic basis identities; (W+A)(W-A)=W^2-A^2;21=12+3+6,42=2*21,9/2=(3/2)*3,126=42*3; and80 summable-tail identities. These checks passed but do not certify this infinite-dimensional theorem. Rerun with python verify_progress.py > verify-progress-run.log. This is substantial scoped proof progress on the genuine nonalgebraizable carrier, and is an unverified draft, not full original P16.7 closure.
